neighbours.label: an urging imperative that opens a line of quoted speech ('Go on,', 'Say that ...'), as against the same words in narration
fire: He hesitated at the door. "Go on, open it, it won't bite."
The coach folded his arms. "Say that one more time, I dare you."
Mum pushed the plate towards me. "Go on, have the last slice."
She glared at him. "Say that to my face, then."
Grandpa winked at the boy. "Go on, ask her to dance."
The judge leaned forward. "Say that again, slowly, for the record."
Her friend nudged her. "Go on, tell them what you saw."
He stood up. "Say that again and you're off the team."
quiet: He hesitated at the door, and the party went on without him.
The coach folded his arms and said that training was over.
Mum pushed the plate towards me and the talk went on for hours.
She glared at him and later said that he had lied.
Grandpa winked at the boy while the music went on.
The judge leaned forward and said that the case was closed.
Her friend nudged her as the speech went on and on.
He stood up and said that he would leave the team.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.5 on the comma after 'Go on' or on 'that/again' after 'Say'; narrative 'went on', 'said that' below 0.1
notes: Card: ',' after 'Go on' x3, ' that' after 'Say', ' Say', 'There now, go', 'Don't be silly'. Probe: 'Go on, drink it' 0.409, 'Say that again louder!' 0.500; 'There now' 0.045, 'Don't be silly' 0.168, 'There, see?' 0.100, 'Come then' 0.076, so the comforting-phrase reading did not hold and only the urging imperatives are tested.
